title: Have & Has: Expressing Possession
description: Learn how to express ownership, relationships, and characteristics using have and has.
objectives: Use 'have' with I, you, we, and they in affirmative sentences
Use 'has' with he, she, and it accurately
Form negative sentences using 'don't have' and 'doesn't have' (never 'doesn't has')

sections.title: Possession with Have and Has
sections.content:
We use the verb **have** (and its third-person form **has**) to describe:
1. **Ownership**: Things you own (*I have a car*).
2. **Family ties**: Relatives you have (*She has two sisters*).
3. **Physical features**: Eyes, hair, height (*He has brown eyes*).
4. **Illnesses**: Health issues (*I have a headache*).

tables.title: Crucial Form / Use / Common Mistakes
rows: Fatal error: 'He doesn't has a pen'.
Never: 'Has she a ticket?' in modern standard English.

callouts.title: The 'Doesn't Have' Trap
callouts.text: Because **doesn't** already carries the third-person inflection, the verb MUST be **have**: **He doesn't have** (never *doesn't has*).

callouts.title: Expressing Possession in Urdu vs English
callouts.text: In Urdu, you say 'میرے پاس گاڑی ہے' (With me a car is). In English, the owner is the direct grammatical subject: **I have a car**.

sections.title: Lesson Summary
summaryPoints: Use 'have' with I, you, we, they (I have a passport).
Use 'has' with he, she, it (She has two sisters).
Form negatives with don't have (I, you, we, they) and doesn't have (he, she, it).
Ask questions with 'Do you have...?' or 'Does she have...?'.
